title: Console request queue: SLA banding and escalation pattern for reporting & exports
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: We receive a continuous stream of console/reporting requests (usage exports, cost breakdowns, bespoke dashboards) from a mix of self-serve users and enterprise customers. Current triage is manual, inconsistent, and causes missed expectations for enterprise SLAs and ops load spikes.

Goal: Define a simple, deterministic SLA-banding and escalation pattern for console/reporting requests that maps incoming requests to delivery lanes (Self-serve / Standard / Enterprise SLA) and prescribes automated escalation steps and data-contract gates. This will reduce mean time to first response, set clear delivery expectations, and reduce PM/eng review cycles for low-risk asks.

Scope (in): classification rules for new console/reporting requests, SLA band definitions and timers, automated routing rules to ticket queues, escalation pattern for overdue items, required metadata/data contracts to start work, sample acceptance criteria, and a rollout path for pilot tenants.

Scope (out): full implementation of new reporting features, UI redesign of the console request form (we will recommend small form changes but not ship a full redesign), billing or rate-limiting policy changes, or changes to backend export pipelines beyond agreed dependency work.

Key decision summary:
- Use three SLA bands: Self-serve (informational / how-to requests, 7d response target), Standard (feature enhancements & small exports, 14d target), Enterprise SLA (contracted, 48h target for first response and 2w delivery target).
- Route to queues based on a lightweight classifier using: request type, workspace tier, monthly spend estimate, frequency signal (repeat request), and a required data-contract checklist field.
- Escalation: T+48h automated nudge to assignee, T+72h route to Ops lead, T+7d PM-level review for re-prioritization. Enterprise SLA items trigger immediate notification to Customer Success on create.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict classifier reduces human overhead but risks misclassification; mitigated by an easy manual re-route workflow and weekly review of false-positive/negative rates.
- Short SLA for enterprise increases engineering context-switching risk; mitigated with a reserved enterprise lane (dedicated rota) and bundling small enterprise fixes into scheduled weekly delivery windows.

Data contracts / mandatory fields to accept a request into Standard/Enterprise lanes:
1) Example dataset or sample rows (or a link to S3/Drive).
2) Intended output format (CSV/Parquet/BigQuery table/dash).
3) Success criteria and stakeholder contact.
4) Privacy/regulatory flag (PII/PHI) — if yes, route to Security review.

Diagnostics & telemetry to measure effectiveness:
- Time to first response by SLA band, backlog depth per band, re-route rate, % of requests missing mandatory fields, engineer time spent per request.
- Goal: reduce time-to-first-response for Enterprise from median 3d to <24h and decrease manual triage volume by 40% in the pilot.
acceptance_criteria: Classifier rules documented and implemented as a simple rule set in the intake service (POC) and tested on past 60 days of tickets to produce banding with >80% match to manual labels
SLA timers and automated escalations implemented in the ticketing system (notifications to assignee, ops lead, PM) and validated with simulated events
Intake form updated with mandatory data-contract fields; form rejects Standard/Enterprise requests missing required fields
Pilot run with two enterprise customers and three internal teams for 4 weeks showing: first response improvement and <15% false classifications
Runbook for re-route and manual override created and published in Confluence with links to dashboards
